system.description: SpaceWire compression node: the images arrive as Space Packets over SpaceWire, the samples of an image in several SDUs of the Octet String Service, the last one marked by the CPTP User Application value 1. The OpenCompact channel compresses every image of 32 x 32 samples in 8 bands of 12 bits losslessly (CCSDS 123.0-B-2, BIP order) and counts the images and the faulty SDUs in its status registers, the OpenCrypto framer cuts every compressed image into chunks, the AES-GCM core encrypts every chunk, and OpenSPP sends every encrypted chunk as one Space Packet back over the same OpenWire port. An ECC monitor reports the corrected and detected errors of the memories of the compressor and of the buffers of the framer. The throughput budget assumes a compression ratio of 2: an assumption about the images, not a property of the channel; the brief marks every number that depends on it.

## 8. Notes from the user guides

**SpaceWire port** (`owr_core`, `spw0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openwire/docs/user_guide.html

- LVDS output buffers for data and strobe and LVDS input buffers with fail-safe biasing belong to the top level; the core contains no I/O buffer.
- Enable the safe implementation of state machines in the synthesis tool.
- Set INT_HOLDOFF and INT_ACK_DELAY for the network before distributed interrupts are used.
- Serve the indication ports before the indication FIFO (16 entries) fills.
- Write registers as 32-bit words; a read that depends on a write waits for the write response.

**N-Char adapter** (`spp_nchar`, `nchar0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openspp/docs/user_guide.html

- A received end of packet marker without data characters is discarded.
- A link packet that ends with a beat without valid bytes gets its marker after the bytes of the earlier beats; a link packet without any byte sends nothing.

**Space Packet node** (`spp_core`, `spp0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openspp/docs/user_guide.html

- Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen.
- After the reset the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles); packets are sent and delivered once the tables are ready.
- Serve every receive port, or place a buffer behind a port whose user can stall for long.
- TxBufferBytes_g holds the longest SDU of a port, RxBufferBytes_g the longest Space Packet.
- Hold the side band (TUser) of a send port constant during an SDU.
- A last beat without valid bytes (Keep all zero) ends an SDU or packet at the inputs; an SDU without any byte is rejected (0x02). The outputs never carry a beat without valid bytes.
- The user supplies the packet secondary header at the start of the Octet String and keeps the secondary header flag of an APID static.

**CCSDS 123.0-B-2 compression channel** (`ocp_channel`, `och0`): https://openspacehdl.org/opencompact/docs/user_guide.html

- Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen with SyncTmr_g = true. A reset aborts the image in progress and clears the counters.
- Every SDU carries a whole number of samples and no other bytes (no secondary header): each sample in a big-endian container of cdiv(D, 8) bytes, the value in its D least significant bits. An SDU with a partial sample ends its image with an error.
- The sender marks the last SDU of every image by the user signal (with OpenSPP: the CPTP User Application value, UserLastMask_g 22x"3FC000", UserLastValue_g 22x"004000" for the value 1); a faulty SDU (UserErrorMask_g, with OpenSPP 22x"003000") ends its image with an error and the SDUs after it up to the next end mark are discarded.
- The status registers count the images (IMAGES_DONE, IMAGES_ABORTED), the faulty and the discarded SDUs (SDU_ERRORS, SDUS_DISCARDED) and the memory errors (ECC_CORRECTED, ECC_UNCORRECTABLE); every counter saturates and a write clears it. IMAGES_DONE + IMAGES_ABORTED is the number of compressed images output.
- An image that ended with a faulty last SDU is complete and has the bytes of a good image; a receiver that must know the faulty images uses Out_Error or the counters.
- The source starts after the reset of the channel with the first SDU of an image; an image in progress at the end of the reset is aborted at its end mark.
- The decompressor must know the tables that are not in the header (table generics false) and the initial accumulators of the hybrid coder.
- The hybrid coder is decoded from the end of the compressed image; keep the end of the packet (Out_Last) up to the decompressor.
- After a detected double error (Ecc_Ded) the compressed image in progress may be wrong; discard it and reset the channel before the next image.
- Enable the TMR of the synthesis tool for the channel; ocp_core protects its memories itself, the adapters and the status registers rely on TMR like all other logic (user guide section 6).

**Chunk framer** (`ocr_framer`, `frm0`): https://openspacehdl.org/opencrypto/docs/user_guide.html

- The slot Cfg_Slot is loaded for generated IVs and stays unchanged while the framer holds chunks.
- Every chunk consumes one invocation of the slot; save the counter regularly (GCM 9.1).
- A receiver decrypts every chunk on its own (IV bytes 0 to 11, AAD bytes 12 to 15, tag the last 16 bytes), orders the chunks by the invocation counter and finds the packet boundaries in the positions.

**AES-GCM core** (`ocr_core`, `ocr0`): https://openspacehdl.org/opencrypto/docs/user_guide.html

- Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen with SyncTmr_g = true.
- After the reset the key table erases every slot (NumKeys_g cycles, STATUS.BUSY = '1'); no key survives a reset.
- One context per message, in the order of the messages; the core pairs the n-th context with the n-th message.
- Load every key slot in use through the registers before sending contexts (programming sequence of the user guide).
- Without the release buffer, discard every decrypted message whose last beat carries the error flag or whose status is not OK.
- Save the invocation counter of every slot with generated IVs regularly ahead of the operational value (GCM 9.1).

**EDAC monitor with registers** (`olo_ft_ecc_monitor_axi`, `edac0`): https://openspacehdl.org/open-logic-ft/doc/ft/olo_ft_ecc_monitor_axi.html

- EDAC monitor with an AXI4-Lite register file and an interrupt.

The system is designed for radiation environments together with the triple modular redundancy (TMR) of the synthesis tool, like the Open Logic ft entities its blocks are built on (`resolved.protection`).

Blocks that protect their memories with SECDED ECC and report it in their registers (the channels count the double-error flags of the status register):

| Block | Channels | Status | Counters | Error injection | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spw0` (`owr_core`) | 6 | `ECC_STATUS` (0x080) | `ECC_SELECT` (0x084), `ECC_COUNT` (0x088) | `ECC_INJECT` (0x08C) | user guide section 5 (protection scope) and the register map |
| `spp0` (`spp_core`) | 8 | `ECC_STATUS` (0x060) | `ECC_SELECT` (0x064), `ECC_COUNT` (0x068) | `ECC_INJECT` (0x06C) | user guide section 6 (protection scope) and the register map |
| `ocr0` (`ocr_core`) | 18 | `ECC_STATUS` (0x0C0) | `ECC_SELECT` (0x0C4), `ECC_COUNT` (0x0C8) | `ECC_INJECT` (0x0CC) | user guide section 6 (protection scope) and the register map |

ECC events of memories (SECDED ECC of the Open Logic ft entities) and where they are reported:

| Source | Memory | Reported at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frm0.Ecc[0]` | chunk buffer of `frm0` | channel 1 of `edac0` (`olo_ft_ecc_monitor_axi`) |
| `frm0.Ecc[1]` | position FIFO of `frm0` | channel 2 of `edac0` (`olo_ft_ecc_monitor_axi`) |
| `och0.Ecc` | memories of the predictor and the entropy coder of ocp_core (channels 0 to 13 of the error injection) of `och0` | channel 0 of `edac0` (`olo_ft_ecc_monitor_axi`) |

State machines recover through their `when others` branch and the reset. All other logic (registers of the control and data paths, counters, pointers, pipeline registers) relies on the TMR of the synthesis tool. The integrator:

- enables the TMR of the synthesis tool for the system,
- checks in the synthesis report that TMR was applied, that the synchroniser chains of the crossings were not triplicated a second time, and that no register-based storage meant to be protected by TMR was inferred as a RAM primitive,
- requests safe state machines, so that synthesis keeps the `when others` branches (AMD Vivado: property `FSM_SAFE_STATE` = `default_state` on the state registers; Synplify: attribute `syn_encoding` = `safe`),
- protects the configuration memory of SRAM-based FPGAs by scrubbing; this is part of the FPGA design.

The ECC paths of the blocks are verified in simulation by error injection. Whether the protection as a whole meets the requirements of a mission is shown by a radiation test of the system in operation.

## 12. Initialisation by software

Register addresses are byte addresses of the AXI4-Lite port of the block; write registers as 32-bit words and wait for the write response before a read that depends on it.

**`spw0`** (SpaceWire port, `owr_core`) through the top-level ports `spw_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x00): it reads 0x4F575201.
2. Optionally write LINK_SPEED (0x14) bits 7:0 RUN_DIV: the bit period in the Run state in LinkClk cycles (reset value RunDiv_g); choose it for the far end, which samples at most about LinkClk / 1.2.
3. Write PORT_CTRL (0x10) = 0x34 (RECEIVER_EN, DRIVER_EN, LINK_START) to start the link, or 0x38 (AUTO_START) to wait for the far end.
4. Wait for PORT_STATUS (0x18) bits 2:0 LINK_STATE = 5 (Run) before packets are exchanged.

**`spp0`** (Space Packet node, `spp_core`) through the top-level ports `spp_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x000): it reads 0x53505001.
2. After the reset wait until TABLE_STATUS (0x040) bits 1:0 (TX_BUSY, RX_BUSY) are 0: the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles).
3. Nothing else is needed: with TxPathDefault_g and RxPathDefault_g every APID has an enabled path to destination 0 and to receive port 0, destination 0 has the Target Logical Address 0xFE (DEST_CTRL 0x400) and the own address is Tla_g. A flight configuration writes the APID tables (TX_TABLE_APID 0x030 and TX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x034, RX_TABLE_APID 0x038 and RX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x03C) and the destinations (DEST_CTRL 0x400 + 0x20 n).

**`och0`** (CCSDS 123.0-B-2 compression channel, `ocp_channel`) through the top-level ports `ocp_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x000): it reads 0x4F435001.
2. None: the channel starts from the initial state of the standard with every image; all parameters are generics. Read ID (0x000) = 0x4F435001 to identify the channel; the configuration registers (0x004 to 0x02C) give the parameters of the compressed images.

**`frm0`** (Chunk framer, `ocr_framer`):

1. Load the key slot Cfg_Slot of the AES-GCM core for generated IVs (KEY_LOAD with IV_GEN = '1', see the core) before the first packet; without a loaded slot every chunk fails with KEY.

**`ocr0`** (AES-GCM core, `ocr_core`) through the top-level ports `ocr_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x000): it reads 0x4F435201.
2. After the reset wait until STATUS (0x014) bit 0 BUSY is 0: the key table erases every slot.
3. Load every key slot in use: write the key to KEY0 to KEY7 (0x040 + 4 n; key byte 4 n in bits 31:24; 4, 6 or 8 words), for generated IVs the fixed field to IV_FIXED (0x060) and the first invocation counter to IV_COUNT_LO (0x064) and IV_COUNT_HI (0x068), then write KEY_LOAD (0x06C) with START (bit 31), IV_GEN (bit 8) and the slot (bits 7:0), for example 0x80000100 for slot 0 with generated IVs; wait until STATUS.BUSY is 0.

## 13. Checks

- Warning: och0.Out feeds frm0.S_In. The error flag of the compressed images (Out_Error on the last beat) is not passed on, so an image that ended with an error (aborted, completed by a faulty SDU, or without its end mark) is sent like a good one. Mark or discard such images by Out_Error, or take them from the counter IMAGES_ABORTED of the status registers.
- Note: ocr0.M_Out has user; spp0.S_Tx[0] gets the side band constants of c7 instead.
- Note: spp0 sends Space Packets of up to ChunkBytes_g + 38 = 4134 bytes: the node that receives them needs RxBufferBytes_g of at least 4134 (spp0 has 8192).
- Note: Packets from the link of spw0 reach spp0.S_Link, which takes at most 8196 bytes: the receive buffer holds the longest Space Packet (error code 0x17); longer ones are discarded.
- Note: No length limit published for spp_nchar (nchar0): packets through it are checked against the other blocks only.

## 14. Verification

A smoke testbench `spw_compression_node_tb` (VHDL-2008, no extra libraries):

1. Instantiate `spw_compression_node` and drive `Clk_sys` at 100 MHz, `Clk_link` at 200 MHz.
2. Hold `Rst` at '1' for 16 cycles of the slowest clock (100 MHz), then '0'.
3. Keep every external input idle: stream inputs with valid at '0', ready inputs of external outputs at '1', bus requests idle, pins at '0'.
4. Run for at least 100 us (the blocks initialise their tables after the reset) and stop the simulation: it must end without failed assertions, and the handshake outputs of the top level (valid, ready) and the line outputs must not be 'U' or 'X' after the reset. Data outputs may stay undefined while their valid is '0'.
5. Where an AXI4-Lite port is external, read the ID register of the block (section 12) and compare it with the documented value.

With GHDL: analyse the libraries of section 1, then `ghdl -i --std=08 -frelaxed spw_compression_node.vhd spw_compression_node_tb.vhd`, `ghdl -m --std=08 -frelaxed spw_compression_node_tb` and `ghdl -r --std=08 -frelaxed spw_compression_node_tb --stop-time=100us --assert-level=error --ieee-asserts=disable` (`--ieee-asserts=disable` silences the warnings of the numeric package about metavalues before the reset).

Optional end-to-end test, after the initialisation of section 12:

- SpaceWire port (`owr_core`): Loop the SpaceWire line back (Spw_DOut to Spw_DIn, Spw_SOut to Spw_SIn) or connect a second port, start the link and wait for PORT_STATUS LINK_STATE = 5 (Run).
- Space Packet node (`spp_core`): Send one SDU on a send port (APID 0x123, for example) and expect it on receive port 0 with the same APID in user bits 10:0, once the APID tables are ready.
- CCSDS 123.0-B-2 compression channel (`ocp_channel`): Send the SDUs of one image, the last one with the end mark, and expect one compressed image at Out without Out_Error; IMAGES_DONE (status registers) counts it.
- AES-GCM core (`ocr_core`): Load the key slot, send a packet and check the output: with generated IVs the first 4 bytes of every message are IV_FIXED, the next 8 the invocation counter; decrypt it with AES-GCM in the test bench (or a second core) and compare.

blocks.name: CCSDS 123.0-B-2 compression channel
blocks.summary: The compressor of ocp_core for a system: the samples of the images arrive as SDUs on a byte stream, for example from a receive port of OpenSPP, every compressed image leaves as one packet of a byte stream, and read-only registers report the configuration and count the images, the faulty and discarded SDUs and the memory errors.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen with SyncTmr_g = true. A reset aborts the image in progress and clears the counters.

Every SDU carries a whole number of samples and no other bytes (no secondary header): each sample in a big-endian container of cdiv(D, 8) bytes, the value in its D least significant bits. An SDU with a partial sample ends its image with an error.

The sender marks the last SDU of every image by the user signal (with OpenSPP: the CPTP User Application value, UserLastMask_g 22x"3FC000", UserLastValue_g 22x"004000" for the value 1); a faulty SDU (UserErrorMask_g, with OpenSPP 22x"003000") ends its image with an error and the SDUs after it up to the next end mark are discarded.

The status registers count the images (IMAGES_DONE, IMAGES_ABORTED), the faulty and the discarded SDUs (SDU_ERRORS, SDUS_DISCARDED) and the memory errors (ECC_CORRECTED, ECC_UNCORRECTABLE); every counter saturates and a write clears it. IMAGES_DONE + IMAGES_ABORTED is the number of compressed images output.
An image that ended with a faulty last SDU is complete and has the bytes of a good image; a receiver that must know the faulty images uses Out_Error or the counters.
The source starts after the reset of the channel with the first SDU of an image; an image in progress at the end of the reset is aborted at its end mark.
The decompressor must know the tables that are not in the header (table generics false) and the initial accumulators of the hybrid coder.
The hybrid coder is decoded from the end of the compressed image; keep the end of the packet (Out_Last) up to the decompressor.
After a detected double error (Ecc_Ded) the compressed image in progress may be wrong; discard it and reset the channel before the next image.
Enable the TMR of the synthesis tool for the channel; ocp_core protects its memories itself, the adapters and the status registers rely on TMR like all other logic (user guide section 6).

rules.message: images of width 1 need reduced prediction and column-oriented local sums (CCSDS 4.3.1, 4.4.1)

The error flag of the compressed images (Out_Error on the last beat) is not passed on, so an image that ended with an error (aborted, completed by a faulty SDU, or without its end mark) is sent like a good one. Mark or discard such images by Out_Error, or take them from the counter IMAGES_ABORTED of the status registers.

init.text: None: the channel starts from the initial state of the standard with every image; all parameters are generics. Read ID (0x000) = 0x4F435001 to identify the channel; the configuration registers (0x004 to 0x02C) give the parameters of the compressed images.

blocks.endToEnd: Send the SDUs of one image, the last one with the end mark, and expect one compressed image at Out without Out_Error; IMAGES_DONE (status registers) counts it.

rates.evidence: the rate data of ocp_core (tools/ocp_throughput.py image_period, tools/ocp_model.py header and max_image_bytes; user guide section 8.1); ocp_channel specification CH-TP-01 and ocp_input_adapter specification IA-FN-05: the samples at the byte rate of the source up to one sample per clock cycle, at most one clock cycle per SDU and one per compressed image

blocks.name: Chunk framer
blocks.summary: Cuts packets of any length into chunks of ChunkBytes_g bytes and hands every chunk to the AES-GCM core as one encryption with a generated IV and a 4-byte AAD with the position of the chunk in its packet.
notes: The slot Cfg_Slot is loaded for generated IVs and stays unchanged while the framer holds chunks.
Every chunk consumes one invocation of the slot; save the counter regularly (GCM 9.1).
A receiver decrypts every chunk on its own (IV bytes 0 to 11, AAD bytes 12 to 15, tag the last 16 bytes), orders the chunks by the invocation counter and finds the packet boundaries in the positions.

rules.message: The framer and the core share clock and reset; a reset of only one of them leaves contexts or messages without partner.

init.text: Load the key slot Cfg_Slot of the AES-GCM core for generated IVs (KEY_LOAD with IV_GEN = '1', see the core) before the first packet; without a loaded slot every chunk fails with KEY.

rates.evidence: TC-FR-03 (four long packets without stall cycles, at most AadBeats + 2 cycles per chunk, hdl/ocr_framer/docs/verification_report.md)

blocks.name: AES-GCM core
blocks.summary: AES-GCM authenticated encryption and decryption (FIPS 197, NIST SP 800-38D, CCSDS 352.0-B-2) with a key table, IV generation per key slot and a register file; one message per context, one status per message.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen with SyncTmr_g = true.
After the reset the key table erases every slot (NumKeys_g cycles, STATUS.BUSY = '1'); no key survives a reset.
One context per message, in the order of the messages; the core pairs the n-th context with the n-th message.
Load every key slot in use through the registers before sending contexts (programming sequence of the user guide).
Without the release buffer, discard every decrypted message whose last beat carries the error flag or whose status is not OK.
Save the invocation counter of every slot with generated IVs regularly ahead of the operational value (GCM 9.1).

rules.message: the AES engine sustains one beat per cycle with ceil(Nr / R) round units and has Nr rounds
the pacer of the key table scrubbers counts milliseconds
the release buffer holds a power of two of at least 16 beats
Set DenseOutput_g = true, so that every message leaves as one gapless byte string (IV, AAD, ciphertext, tag); the sectioned output is for the input of a second core (decryption).

The error flag of the messages (user bit 2 on the last beat) is not passed on, so a message that failed (for example with KEY) is sent like a good one. Set ReleaseBuffer_g = true (a message leaves the core only when its status is OK) with ReleaseBytes_g a power of two that holds the longest message in whole beats (IV, AAD, data and tag each start a new beat), or consume the status at M_Sts.

init.text: After the reset wait until STATUS (0x014) bit 0 BUSY is 0: the key table erases every slot.

Load every key slot in use: write the key to KEY0 to KEY7 (0x040 + 4 n; key byte 4 n in bits 31:24; 4, 6 or 8 words), for generated IVs the fixed field to IV_FIXED (0x060) and the first invocation counter to IV_COUNT_LO (0x064) and IV_COUNT_HI (0x068), then write KEY_LOAD (0x06C) with START (bit 31), IV_GEN (bit 8) and the slot (bits 7:0), for example 0x80000100 for slot 0 with generated IVs; wait until STATUS.BUSY is 0.

blocks.endToEnd: Load the key slot, send a packet and check the output: with generated IVs the first 4 bytes of every message are IV_FIXED, the next 8 the invocation counter; decrypt it with AES-GCM in the test bench (or a second core) and compare.

rates.evidence: TC-CO-10 and TC-CO-11 (back-to-back encryptions and decryptions without stall cycles, hdl/ocr_core/docs/verification_report.md)

M_Out.cycles: DenseOutput_g * (cdiv(n, B) + 1) + (1 - DenseOutput_g) * (cdiv(12, B) + cdiv(n - 28, B) + cdiv(16, B))

sizes.evidence: user guide section 2 (generics LenBits_g and ReleaseBytes_g) and section 8 (the release buffer holds the longest message); the cycles of a release buffer that holds one message but not two: user guide section 7.1, TC-CO-15 (the bound max(B + 2, 3 M - D + 4) for M sectioned beats in a buffer of D beats) and TC-CO-16 (framer chunks of 4096 bytes at 128 bit, hdl/ocr_core/docs/verification_report.md)
